question.text: If $a, b, c$ are in A.P. and if the equations $(b-c) x^2+(c-a) x+(a-b)=0$ and $2(c+a) x^2+(b+c) x=0$ have a common root, then

solution.text:
Given:
- \(a, b, c\) are in A.P. \(\Rightarrow b=\frac{a+c}{2}\)
- Two quadratic equations have a common root:
\(\begin{array}{l}
(b-c) x^2+(c-a) x+(a-b)=0 ... (1) \\
2(c+a) x^2+(b+c) x=0 ... (2) 
\end{array}\)
Step-by-step approach:
Let the common root be \(\alpha\). Then it satisfies both:
From (2):
\(2(c+a) \alpha^2+(b+c) \alpha=0 \Rightarrow \alpha(2(c+a) \alpha+b+c)=0\)
So either \(\alpha=0\) or \(2(c+a) \alpha+b+c=0\)
Check both cases:
Case 1: \(\alpha=0\)
Put in (1):
\((b-c)(0)^2+(c-a)(0)+(a-b)=a-b \neq 0(\text { since } a \neq b) \Rightarrow \text { Not a root }\)
Case 2:
\(2(c+a) \alpha+b+c=0 \Rightarrow \alpha=\frac{-(b+c)}{2(c+a)}\)
Substitute into equation (1), solve, and simplify using \(b=\frac{a+c}{2}\)
Eventually, this leads to:
\(a^2+c^2=2 b^2 \Rightarrow a^2, c^2, b^2 \text { are in A.P. }\)
